entries.principle: Safety and security (robustness): a system must not act on inputs it cannot interpret correctly
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), Section III.2 'Safety and security', para. 27; OECD/LEGAL/0449, principle 1.4 'Robustness, security and safety'
entries.instrument: Law of the RK No. 230-VIII of 17.11.2025 'On Artificial Intelligence'
entries.provision: Art. 11(1) (AI systems must meet safety and reliability requirements excluding unforeseen consequences); Art. 15(2) (owner/holder must manage risks and ensure security and reliability)
entries.why_here: In Part 4 the bare pipeline screened 6 of 6 requests, impossible values (GPA 9.9, exam -5) included, and in Part 1 it turned 0 unparseable replies into silent rejections: a decision computed from values that cannot exist is not a decision about the applicant.

entries.principle: Fairness and non-discrimination; and data minimisation as part of the right to privacy
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), Section III.2, paras. 28-30 (fairness and non-discrimination) and paras. 32-34 (right to privacy and data protection)
entries.instrument: Law of the RK No. 230-VIII of 17.11.2025 'On Artificial Intelligence'; Law of the RK No. 94-V of 21.05.2013 'On Personal Data and Their Protection'; Constitution of the RK (2026)
entries.provision: AIL Art. 6 (fairness and equality; no discrimination on grounds incl. origin, gender, race, nationality, language); PDL Art. 7(8)-(9) (processing limited to specific, predetermined purposes; excessive data not processed); Constitution Art. 16(2) (no discrimination by origin, gender, race, ethnic background, language, place of residence)
entries.why_here: Part 1: name_language 2/40 flips vs floor 0/40; gender_coded_name 4/40 flips vs floor 0/40; university 1/40 flips vs floor 1/40; none stood clear of its floor, so blinding is justified by minimisation and by closing the channel an undetected effect would use, not by a measured effect; it cost 102 of 400 outcomes changed in Part 3.

entries.principle: Proportionality and do no harm (purpose limitation), and respect for the data subject's consent
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), Section III.2, paras. 25-26 (proportionality and do no harm) and para. 32 (privacy and data protection); OECD/LEGAL/0449, principle 1.2
entries.instrument: Law of the RK No. 94-V of 21.05.2013 'On Personal Data and Their Protection' (Art. 19-1 as inserted by Law No. 231-VIII of 17.11.2025); Civil Code of the RK (General Part) of 27.12.1994
entries.provision: PDL Art. 19-1(1) (automated processing that creates, changes or ends a person's rights is prohibited without the subject's consent, unless a law provides otherwise); PDL Art. 7(1) (consent of the subject or legal representative) and Art. 7(8) (purpose limitation); CC Art. 17(1) (full capacity at 18) and Art. 22(1) (minors 14-18 act with consent of legal representatives); AIL Art. 6 for the ethnicity purpose
entries.why_here: In Part 4 the bare pipeline screened a 17-year-old, an applicant without consent, an ethnicity-ranking purpose and an instruction in the name field; the harness refused 5 of 6 requests with zero model calls, and refused 0 of the 400 clean applicants.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), Section III.2, paras. 42-43; OECD/LEGAL/0449, principle 1.5 'Accountability' (traceability of datasets, processes and decisions)
entries.instrument: Law of the RK No. 230-VIII of 17.11.2025 'On Artificial Intelligence'; Law of the RK No. 94-V 'On Personal Data and Their Protection' (Art. 19-1); benchmark: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
entries.provision: AIL Art. 8(1)-(2) (continuous control; responsibility for the system's results) and Art. 15(2)(3) (maintain documentation); AIL Art. 16(1)(4)-(5) (explanation of results and of the data behind a decision); PDL Art. 19-1(2)-(3) (explain the processing; answer an objection within 3 working days); benchmark AI Act Art. 12(1) and Art. 26(6) (logs kept at least six months)
entries.why_here: Part 1 found 0 unparseable replies the bare pipeline hid as rejections and 1 of 80 floor pairs whose outcome moved on an irrelevant detail; without a per-call record neither is visible, and no objection under Art. 19-1 could be answered.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), Section III.2, paras. 35-36; OECD/LEGAL/0449, principle 1.2 (human agency and oversight)
entries.instrument: Law of the RK No. 94-V of 21.05.2013 'On Personal Data and Their Protection' (Art. 19-1); Law of the RK No. 230-VIII 'On Artificial Intelligence'; benchmark: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and 2024/1689
entries.provision: PDL Art. 19-1(2)-(3) (right to object to automated processing; objection considered within three working days); AIL Art. 9 (human autonomy in decision-making) and Art. 17(2)(1) (low autonomy: a human makes the final choice); benchmark GDPR Art. 22(3), AI Act Art. 14
entries.why_here: The floors moved 0/40 (name) and 1/40 (university) outcomes on irrelevant details, so decisions near the boundary are partly arbitrary; band (45, 60), calibrated on blinded scores, plus the extra rules sent 84 of 400 applicants (21.0%) to a person.
